title: Do anyone ever tried to change a single thing and the entire game just fucking broke?
author: TayrusOkami
selftext: Coding my physical TCG into a virtual game, tried to tweak the main menu and then the gameplay was all affected, wtf man 😭😭

comments.author: Reckonerxy
comments.body: thats why you always have to playtest your game first after every change.

replies.author: TayrusOkami
replies.body: I did, that's why I got so confused.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: Install and learn to use git, it will save you endless hours of frustration.

replies.author: TayrusOkami
replies.body: Frustration is my word of the year, apparently

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body:
So one of the things I learned as someone who started coding in the 80s, you need to make lots of documentation.

A tip is when you ask the agent to do something, include these 1) ask the agent to record everything it does to a markdown file inside the project root folder (like the docs folder), and 2) have it write a summary of the work it's done and the files it touched to a 'chanfges.md' file which is an industry standard for tracking changes to a project so handing it off to another coder/studio is easy peasy, 3) use git, have the agent create a git commit with a proper comment after each and every session. 

This will permit you to go back and review what went wrong, and permit reversions easily if something is amiss. You can also ask the agent to comp\[are git commits and locate the issue to correct it as long as you've got the documentation to give it context. 

My mantra - document, document, and then document some more. 

Be well and keep creating.

replies.author: TayrusOkami
replies.body: Thank you, I'll use that mantra too lmao
